name: AnubisAboveBelow
source:
As Above So Below. 
 
 `` Remember the most important rule'', Anubis growled, his eyes shimmering in the cold light. `` As above, so below'' I shook my head. 
 
 `` Do you think I'm crazy?'' I asked him. The jackal god shook his head, sweeping his jaw back and forth. 
 
 `` I do n't think you're crazy, Steven'', he replied. `` I think you're greedy and selfish. Just like most other humans.'' I shrugged, and waved him off. 
 
 `` I'll see you in a hundred years'', I rasped, dismissively. 
 
 I walked across the interior of the spacecraft, and through the vestibule. The door shot closed with a swoosh. The light of the tremendous blue planet below hit my eyes. I settled down into the control seat, and swiped at the console. Four green and yellow continents shrouded by swirling white clouds twinkled up. 
 
 The pod detached itself from the mothership with a whir and a thrum. It blasted down toward the planet. The pod rumbled as we descended through the atmosphere, piercing through the blankets of cloud. 
 
 We shot over a rocky desert pockmarked with craters and gnarled canyons. Sandstone outcrops spiked up hundreds of metres into the air. Dotted about over the rocks were dense blasts of alien foliage: trees which sprouted branches at unnatural angles, puffy green cacti, and dazzling neon whirls of shrubbery. 
 
 Beyond the desert lay green, grassy plains dotted with what looked like alien sunflowers. A broad blue river cut down from snowy-capped mountains in the distance. The river led to a foamy blue ocean. I put the pod down at the head of a bay over a stiff igneous cliff. I snapped up the visor of my thin silvery spacesuit, flipped the lid of the pod and hauled myself out onto the grassy verge. 
 
 As above so below? No. I do n't think so. This is my world. This planet belongs to *me*. None of the bastards at the academy can tell me what to do anymore. I am no longer bound by their stupid rules about spreading freedom and equality across the galaxy. 
 
 I cracked a fierce grin. I reached into the pouch of my spacesuit, and pulled out the shiny colony drone. I threw it up into the air. Its exterior shell cracked, spitting out a complex whirl of lights. Trillions of tiny microdrones cracked out, bursting into the air. They shot off—up into the sky, down into the soil. They would hunt materials to build more drones. Bigger drones. Construction drones that could put up great towering cities. Atmospheric drones that could alter the air content to make it breathable. And population drones that could incubate and birth humans and animals. 
 
 I swiped at my neural interface, tweaking the programming. 
 
 I clambered back into the pod. I swooped the lid shut. I flicked through the neural interface, and put myself to sleep for a year. 
 
 *** 
 
 I awoke beneath a towering quartz skyscraper filled with big, bright windows rose miles into the air above the pod. A few smaller towers clustered about it. 
 
 Construction was ongoing. Hordes of blue crablike drones crawled about the exterior of the buildings, shooting construction materials out of their bellies, printing up the cityscape. 
 
 I cracked the lid and clambered out, looking about the newly formed plaza. Planted trees—ash, silver birch, sycamore—swayed in the ocean breeze. 
 
 I checked the air levels. It was breathable. I took my helmet off, and placed it on the ground. I tasted the salty air for the first time. I walked across to the high tower. The door swept upwards with a whoosh, leading to a bright, light atrium, paved with marble and flowing with gilded accoutrements. I walked across to the line of elevators at the back. I entered one on the right, and swiped at the console. The elevator blasted downward. 
 
 I emerged into a dark chamber with a cold metal floor. Rows of green glowing vats spread out as far as the eye could see, each filled with a naked, growing human. Their eyes were open, unflinching, unblinking. My personal army. Finally. They belong to me. They serve only me. 
 
 What could possibly go wrong? 
 
 I took the elevator back up to the top floor. The door opened with a swoosh. My gilded throne room lay about ahead. It was a plush apartment, expansive and open. On the right stood a glossy white grand piano, a heart-shaped swimming pool. On the left was a towering grey holoscreen, lined with rows of seating. Bookshelves containing thousands and thousands of books lined the walls. Between the bookshelves stood thick mahogany doors. 
 
 Grecian statues lined the pathway up to the gleaming golden throne. I walked up, and took my seat. I slouched down into its cold arms, looking out over the grassy plains, toward the mountains over my dominion. New forests of Earth trees had been planted up across the plains to oxygenate the atmosphere. 
 
 I walked over to the holoscreen, and flicked it on. Only a few days to wait. 
 
 The birthings will begin soon. 
 
 *** 
 
 I stood in front of the glowing green vat as it belched out the man with a squelch. He was a blonde man with big green eyes. He coughed and rasped, sucking in his first breaths of air. 
 
 `` Get up!'' I sneered at him. `` Get up and serve your king!'' His eyes were wide. He jumped to his feet. 
 
 `` Yes your highness!'' he barked, still dripping with the viscous green liquid from the vat. His face was docile and compliant. `` What can I do to serve you?'' 
 
 `` Follow'' I told him. We walked back to the elevator. We took it up to the top, to my apartment. He followed me out acoss the floor, toward the throne, and out onto the balcony, into the midmorning sunshine. 
 
 I had to test him. I had to make sure that the programming had worked. `` Throw yourself off'' I commanded. 
 
 `` Off?'' he asked. 
 
 `` Down to the dust.'' 
 
 He nodded, grimly and took a flying leap over the fence. I watched him plummet downward falling into the plaza below with a tremendous splat. Rosy gore splashed about. I grinned. 
 
 As above so below, my ass. 
 
 *** 
 
 I watched from the balcony. There were thousands of them now. My loyal subjects. They teemed about in the mud between the rows of wooden huts that sprawled out below my high tower. A little shanty town. 
 
 I kept them poor. It toughened their spirits. They had to hunt game for food in forests below. They had to grow crops in the criss-cross patchwork quilt of fields. Meanwhile I tucked into banquets from the tower's replicators. 
 
 I made sure they knew what happened if they ever crossed their king. 
 
 Anubis would be furious. So would my classmates at the academy. But this is not their concern. 
 
 This is my planet. 
 
 And I do what I want.
retelling:
Narrator: Anubis, the jackal god, witnessing the cosmic dance from his timeless realm, observed a peculiar event unfold in the vast expanse of the universe.

On this day, a mortal named Steven, filled with ambition and disregard for the divine decree, "As above, so below," ventured forth into the unknown. Accompanied by his faithful colony drone, he descended upon an alien planet, defying the academy's directives.

From my perspective, I watched as this mortal manipulated the landscape, constructing a city of quartz and glass that towered above the barren desert and lush grasslands. The river that flowed from the snowy mountains to the blue ocean served as a lifeline for his new domain, and the vast, igneous cliff provided a suitable landing pad for his space pod.

Yet, it was not just the physical structures that he sought to control; Steven also commanded the lives of the beings who inhabited this world. His solution: vats filled with human embryos, nurtured and grown to serve him. The underground chamber buzzed with the hum of life as these beings took their first breaths, unaware of the fate that awaited them.

The mortal Steven, seduced by power, crowned himself ruler over this world, establishing a kingdom of opulence atop his quartz skyscraper. His throne room shimmered with gold and glittering holoscreens, while below him lay the shanty town - a stark reminder of the impoverished lives of his subjects.

As I watched this spectacle unfold, my heart heavy with sorrow, I could not help but feel the weight of what this mortal had wrought. His disobedience and tyranny defied the principles of the academy that once trained him. And yet, he stood defiant, asserting his dominion over this new world, uttering the chilling words, "This is my planet. And I do what I want."

As the story continues to unfold from the eyes of Anubis, the jackal god, one can only wonder at the consequences that will befall this mortal who dared to challenge the natural order.
